why_trail.why: Handoff is complete and authoritative. One handoff error found: it locates test_a_missing_journal_is_covered_by_the_second_witness in tests/test_episode_capture.py; the code has it in tests/test_episode_fields.py:383. Code wins.

Two tests in EscalatedReopenIsNotAReopenTests reach a real rework-cap escalation through the real CLI and read the seam-emitted snapshot. Reopen seam needs E=2 because the in-flight journal line is missing, which exactly cancels a single escalation - a reopen-only test would have passed on the broken code.

Fix B landed entirely inside scripts/episode_capture.py: reopen_total(checklist) now sums per-task rework_count alone; journal_reopens and find_spine_path deleted with the spine_path plumbing through mechanical_fields. Engine journalling untouched. The docstring states the deliberate under-count cost on the amend-drops-a-gate path.

Both named sites corrected, and a repo-wide sweep for over-count/under-count/two-witnesses prose found no third site. episode_capture.py's reopen_total docstring now names the escalation branch as the over-counting mechanism; ReopensFieldTests' class docstring and the ex-missing-journal test docstring both say the journal over-counts and point at the killing test.

All three corrections independently re-measured before writing, not copied: setdefault(refusals,0) is at checklist_engine.py:964 inside claim() which starts at :894; frobnicate exits 2 with the counter unmoved; a foreign --session-id start takes exit 1 and moves the owning checklist 0 to 1. Doc now says checklist-scoped with the foreign-session caveat stated, drops the malformed-verb example, and distinguishes the CLI-boundary increments from the in-claim arming. Counting semantics unchanged.
